images.title: Trap √52 between 7 and 8
images.purpose: Shows √52 trapped in the band between 7 and 8 on a number line, since 7² = 49 and 8² = 64, so 52 is not a perfect square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One horizontal number line segment with a shaded band, a flag near the left bound, and two squarings beneath.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal number line with exactly 2 labelled ticks, 7 at the left and 8 at the right, far apart. The band between them is shaded light teal (#0072B2). A reddish purple (#CC79A7) flag stands on the line about one fifth of the way from 7 to 8, labelled √52. Under the 7 tick: 7² = 49. Under the 8 tick: 8² = 64. Above the band, centred: not a perfect square. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A number whose root is trapped strictly between two whole numbers is not a perfect square.
images.description: Shows √52 trapped in the band between 7 and 8 on a number line, since 7² = 49 and 8² = 64, so 52 is not a perfect square.
images.context: √52 ≈ 7.21. Neutral number, not one of the practice questions.

image_decisions.why: The tool's core move is setting two whole number bounds whose squares trap the number.
